title: Low-register playing with a derby mute
summary: Allen recalls the Charlie Love record session; Barnes explains his low-register clarinet played into a felt derby, which no one else did until his records.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: You know that time you cut the records with Charlie Love? Do you remember that? Was it on St. Louis Street near Decatur? That's right, yeah. Uh huh. Well it seemed to me as the evening went on, you changed your whole tone and style and everything, you know? Yeah. You played different. You played different that night from any other time I heard you. I don't think they issued the stuff, you know, late in the evening where you began to play very different.
Uh huh. Well I, I don't know. I played different always.
Where did you get your low register ideas? Is that all you're on?

That's all my home. That's all my home. Low right of stone. They can take the low register. And uh, the door that's covered as a man trumpet, cover the trumpet. You got a way down on bass baritone tone on there. Way deep. It's a joy. You can probably feel the joy on the floor if you're sitting there. I don't see none of them do it yet.
Well how does that work? Oh, that works pretty good. I mean how do you do that? I don't get the picture. You just play low?
Just play low. Right in low register. You use the derby as a mute.
Take your horn and put right down the door. Is that a felt derby like or a metal derby? Felt derby like. Just like you were on your head. Whatever derbies are made out of, I never thought about.

Did any other clarinet players do that besides you? None of them ain't never seen it down there. They ain't gonna do it. That's the way I feel about it. They ain't never played low register till I started putting their hold it on the record, got it, and most of them use it. Those men would all of this hit it and go, but they wouldn't get on in it. They'd just catch a little redstone, play in it, half wind low, half sound.
